evidence: Melle Mel was an MC for Grandmaster Flash, in the group recorded as Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, and the routines the group developed around Flash's DJing are documented throughout hip-hop histories and the group's own recordings from 1979 onward.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Listen to how the five MCs hand lines to each other, finishing each other's bars and coming in together on the last word. That is choreography built for a live room where the DJ is the main event and the MCs work around him, and you can hear it surviving intact onto a record where there is no room and no crowd.

explanation.age7: He started out as one of the voices talking over Flash's records at parties.
explanation.age13: Melle Mel was one of five MCs who performed with Grandmaster Flash. Their routines were worked out for live parties, with lines passed between them and everyone landing together on the last word, all built around Flash's DJing. When they started making records that choreography came with them, even though a record has no crowd to work.
explanation.adult: Included because it establishes what Mel was formed by before 'The Message' asks something different of him. The Furious Five's group technique is a live-performance artefact, and its persistence on record is a good example of a form outliving the conditions that produced it.
